headline_marked: Trump announces [[complete disarmament of Hamas]] for Gaza peace
headline: Trump announces complete disarmament of Hamas for Gaza peace
summary: The agreement involves the decommissioning of weapons in structured phases, coinciding with a gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from the Gaza Strip.
details: US President Donald Trump announced a historic agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza, calling it a monumental step toward lasting peace and security.

The deal, reached through mediators from Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey, involves the decommissioning of weapons in carefully structured phases. As disarmament is completed, Israeli forces will gradually withdraw from the territory.
A new Palestinian police force and an International Stabilization Force (ISF) will work together to take over security responsibilities, ensuring Gaza is safe for its residents and neighbors.
The plan also establishes the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), a group of Palestinian technocrats who will assume day-to-day governance during the transitional phase.

The roadmap includes the elimination of all tunnels, weapons depots, and production facilities, with all weapons—heavy and light—falling under the full control of the NCAG in coordination with the ISF.

While Hamas officials confirmed an agreement on weapons and Israeli withdrawal, some Israeli political sources claim the deal does not yet satisfactorily address all their demands for full demilitarization.
Despite the ceasefire, violence continues in Gaza, with health officials reporting at least four people killed in Israeli strikes on Thursday.
caption:
A historic deal for the complete disarmament of Hamas has been announced. Is this the path to lasting peace in Gaza?

US President Donald Trump announced a historic agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza, calling it a monumental step toward lasting peace and security.

The deal, reached through mediators from Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey, involves the decommissioning of weapons in carefully structured phases. As disarmament is completed, Israeli forces will gradually withdraw from the territory.

A new Palestinian police force and an International Stabilization Force (ISF) will work together to take over security responsibilities, ensuring Gaza is safe for its residents and neighbors.

The plan also establishes the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), a group of Palestinian technocrats who will assume day-to-day governance during the transitional phase.

The roadmap includes the elimination of all tunnels, weapons depots, and production facilities, with all weapons—heavy and light—falling under the full control of the NCAG in coordination with the ISF.

While Hamas officials confirmed an agreement on weapons and Israeli withdrawal, some Israeli political sources claim the deal does not yet satisfactorily address all their demands for full demilitarization.

Despite the ceasefire, violence continues in Gaza, with health officials reporting at least four people killed in Israeli strikes on Thursday.

headline_marked: US Special Envoy [[Sergio Gor to visit Rohingya camps]] in Cox's Bazar
headline: US Special Envoy Sergio Gor to visit Rohingya camps in Cox's Bazar
summary: The US President's Special Envoy for South and Central Asia is visiting Bangladesh to assess the situation of Rohingya refugees.
details: US President's Special Envoy for South and Central Asia, Sergio Gor, is heading to Cox's Bazar to visit Rohingya refugee camps.
Gor is scheduled to fly directly from Dhaka to Cox's Bazar on Friday, July 31, to assess the overall situation of the refugees.
Prior to this, he arrived in Dhaka on Thursday afternoon and held a meeting with Foreign Minister Dr. Khalilur Rahman at the State Guest House Padma.
Following the meeting, the Foreign Minister stated that the relationship between the current government and the United States has been strong from the start and is continuing to strengthen.
Bangladesh has requested the United States to increase its assistance for the Rohingya refugees.
Sergio Gor's three-day mission to Bangladesh will conclude after a meeting with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday.
caption:
US Special Envoy Sergio Gor is visiting Rohingya camps in Cox's Bazar to assess the refugee crisis.

US President's Special Envoy for South and Central Asia, Sergio Gor, is heading to Cox's Bazar to visit Rohingya refugee camps.

Gor is scheduled to fly directly from Dhaka to Cox's Bazar on Friday, July 31, to assess the overall situation of the refugees.

Prior to this, he arrived in Dhaka on Thursday afternoon and held a meeting with Foreign Minister Dr. Khalilur Rahman at the State Guest House Padma.

Following the meeting, the Foreign Minister stated that the relationship between the current government and the United States has been strong from the start and is continuing to strengthen.

Bangladesh has requested the United States to increase its assistance for the Rohingya refugees.

Sergio Gor's three-day mission to Bangladesh will conclude after a meeting with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday.
